source_title: Patrick Stewart Made Final Public Appearance 2 Years Before His Death - People.com
source_excerpt:
The actor, who died at 86 on Oct. 28, was last seen publicly supporting his beloved Huddersfield Town at a soccer match in England
Patrick Stewart attended a Huddersfield Town match in November 2024, supporting the team he loved since childhood
The actor died at home in Los Angeles on Wednesday, Oct. 28
Stewart was known for Star Trek and X-Men roles alongside acclaimed Shakespearean stage work
Patrick Stewart spent his final public appearance supporting a sports team he had loved since childhood.
The legendary Star Trek and X-Men actor, who died at age 86 on Wednesday, Oct. 28, was last spotted publicly attending Huddersfield Town’s match against Crawley Town at Broadfield Stadium in Crawley, England, on Nov. 9, 2024.
Wearing a blue-and-white Huddersfield scarf over a coat, Stewart was photographed smiling in the stands with one hand raised at the time.
The star last posed for photos at an event during Netflix’s The Piano Lesson tastemaker screening at Ross House in Los Angeles on Oct. 19, 2024.
His final Instagram post came this year on Oct. 16, when he posted about potentially earning a Grammy nomination for his recording of Shakespeare’s sonnets.
“Delighted to learn that @simon.audio have submitted my audiobook of Shakespeare’s sonnets for Grammy consideration,” he wrote in the caption at the time. “I think The Bard would love a Grammy!” (Nominations will be announced on Nov. 16.)
His devotion to the club stretched back decades. In a 2017 interview with Sky Sports , Stewart recalled his uncle Arnold taking him to his first match at age 7.
“Huddersfield has always been my club. I watch every match, usually 24 hours later,” he said in 2023, according to Huddersfield Hub .
Stewart died at his Los Angeles home with his wife Sunny Ozell by his side following a “brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” according to a statement from his longtime spokesperson, Kelly Bush Novak.
“He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all,” the statement added. “We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace.”
The statement also noted that the actor was a “lifelong Huddersfield Football fan.”
Best known for portraying Capt. Jean-Luc Picard in the Star Trek franchise and Professor Charles Xavier in Marvel’s X-Men films, Stewart also earned acclaim for his work onstage, particularly in Shakespeare’s plays. His theater career included performances with the Royal Shakespeare Company and Broadway productions of Macbeth and Waiting for Godot . He’ll reprise his X-Men role in Avengers: Doomsday , in theaters this Dec. 18.
